question: Should live failed-patch diagnostics be required to use supported Codex `PostToolUse` or app-server events, or may this plugin scan private rollout JSONL during event projection as a temporary fallback?
rationale: The choice defines a security-sensitive and availability-sensitive runtime boundary that repository policy and tests alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Require event-native diagnostics
options.body: Remove the rollout scanner and extend the supported native hook or app-server projection to carry the required bounded fields.

options.title: Accept a temporary scanner
options.body: Retain the scanner only with explicit owner approval plus live redaction, slow-storage, version-drift, and rollout-disabled proof.

options.title: Pause for upstream support
options.body: Defer the diagnostics until Codex exposes the missing failure details through a stable app-server or hook contract.

recommendation.title: Require event-native diagnostics
recommendation.body: Remove the rollout scanner and extend the supported native hook or app-server projection to carry the required bounded fields.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex app-server liveness and integration work makes this the strongest available owner for deciding whether live filesystem inspection is acceptable.
